Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 18 May 1990, after the 
draft finalized by the Inland and Harbour Crafts Sectional Committee had been approved by 
Transport Engineering Division Council. 

Floaters for dredgers are used mainly for float pipes of the delivery piping system. In order that 
such floaters could be manufactured of proper quality, this Indian Standard has been formulated 
for the guidance of manufacturers and users. 

In the formulation of this standard assistance has been derived from JIS> F 3994 : 1979 'Dredgers 
Floaters' issued by Japanese Industrial Standards Committee. 



AMENDMENT NO. 1 AUGUST 1997 

TO

is a necessary adjunct to this standard'." 

( Page 1, clause 4.1 , line 2 ) — Substitute 'conforming to grade A of IS 
2062* for 'to designation Fe4l05 of IS 226 : 1975*.

IS 12963 : 1990 



Indian Standard 



INLAND VESSELS — DREDGERS- 
FLOATERS— SPECIFICATION 



1 SCOPE 

1.1 This standard lays down the requirements 
for floaters for dredgers used mainly for float 
pipes of dredger's delivery piping system. 

2 REFERENCE 

2.1 IS 226 : 1975 Structural steel (standard 
quality) {fifth revision) is a necessary adjunct to 
this standard 

3 DIMENSIONS 

3.1 The dimensions of floaters shall be as given 
in Table I read with Fig. 1- 

4 MATERIAL 

4.1 The floaters shall be manufactured from 
steel to designation Fe4105 of IS 226 ■ 1975. 



5 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS 

5.1 The component parts of the floaters shall be 
free from flaws, cracks or other defects. The 
floaters shall he coated with suitable atiti- 
cot tosive paint. 

6 DESIGNATION 

6*1 The floaters shall be designated by name 

and nominal size. 

7 PERFORMANCE TESTS 

7.1 The floater shall be subjected to the test 
piessure of 01 MPa ( 1 kgf/em'* ) for a period of 
5 minutes At the end of the test, the floater 
shall not show any Mgn of leakage. 

8 MARKING 

8*1 The floater shall be marked with the 
nominal size., ye;u of manufacture and indi- 
cation of source of manufacture.

Staadard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by [he provisions of the Bureau of indutn Standards 
Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products 
covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with 
the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality 
control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked 
products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safe- 
guard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted 
to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 



mmt lamina 

BIS ii a itatutory institut ion established under the Bursau of Indian Standards Act* 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification 
of goods and attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in 
any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in 
the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or 
grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director ( Publications ) t 

Revision of Indian Standard! 

Indian Standards are reviewed periodically and revised, when necessary and amendments, if any, 
are issued from time to time. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in 
possession of the latest amendments or edition. Comments on this Indian Standard may be sent 
to BIS giving the following reference:
